sourceInformation.genre: Arcade flight action, station shooting and light mission planning
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person pilot and four gun stations, downward bombsight, overhead operational map, exterior reveals
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (8ecc2f6) + native World3D; Three.js 0.182.0; Rapier 0.19.3; JavaScript/Web Audio; Bun 1.3.14 single-file bundle
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural chunky PS1/N64 geometry, olive aircraft, amber instruments and a blue Channel
sourceInformation.animation: Native World3D pen, continuous math poses, native Humanoid radio portraits and fixed-step aircraft animations
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized music, engines, weapons, flak and Animalese-style radio gibberish; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 local couch co-op (keyboard+pad or two pads); AI Hub Session Protocol v1 shared-world, client 1.4.0. Standalone internet room hosting: none.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless deterministic simulation, actual native keyboard/mouse whole sortie, standard-pad stubs, Chromium touch emulation, Chromium/WebKit file-origin rendering, OfflineAudioContext, five AI Hub harness scenarios including latency/loss and playerless server. No physical controller, touch device or listener.
sourceInformation.research: Read preserved Blue Sky Rangers original instructions and developer history; inspected Intv Funhouse source screenshots. Original audio recordings/timbres: unknown; new music, SFX and gibberish are original.

testingFeedback: 40 distinct implementation issues were corrected during automated checks, code audits and screenshot review; the closed ledger is docs/issues.md. Test-driver errors and environment limits are excluded.
4 critical startup, core-rendering or two-view co-op or stranded-menu blockers were corrected. No known release-blocking issue remains.
The complete public keyboard/mouse sortie, nine loadout/difficulty full sorties and actual multi-client Hub harness were most useful because they exercised coupled systems and cleanup.
An immediate screenshot during the native menu opening animation showed a transient empty panel; a settled screenshot was needed to assess the actual briefing.
engineFeedback: Native World3D pen, shapes, independent cameras and fixed-step E.Game made a coherent procedural aircraft and split views possible.
The native overlay skips split views, and first-person geometry placed in the large world could disappear in one pane. Separate native camera-space overlays resolved it.
Coupled bomber flight, resources, station authority, bombing ballistics, damage and complete sortie orchestration.
Portable bundling and stable independent first-person overlays across two viewports, with correct station/input ownership.

No upstream engine source edits. Added game systems, two native camera-space overlay scenes with per-viewport rendering, input/Shell adaptations, portable bundling and standard missing GPU constants for import compatibility.
Make per-viewport first-person overlays and their camera frame a documented public rendering path.
promptFeedback: The complete sortie loop and exact handoff schema gave the build a clear destination.
The source jettisons fuel while PLAN deliberately specifies payload jettison; this adaptation follows PLAN.
Preserving one authoritative aircraft and station/input ownership across solo, couch co-op, file origin and AI Hub.
Separate acceptance gates from optional polish and specify one expected evidence format.

aiHub.name: B-17 Cross Channel Chaos
aiHub.tagline: One bomber. Six stations. Bring everyone home.
aiHub.description: Command a vulnerable four-engine bomber across the Channel. Defend four bearings, line up a military harbor strike, and get the crew home, solo or with a second crew member.
aiHub.controls: WASD fly, E/Q power, 1/2/3 stations, mouse aim, click/Space fire/release, M map, H hold; pad sticks, R2, Triangle, Square, L1/R1.
